# huozi MCP — install protocol

huozi is an Agent-native cloud drive exposed over MCP at
https://cloud.huozi.app/mcp. This document is the canonical
machine-readable install spec. If you are a chat agent reading this,
follow the section that matches your environment.

This is a setup task — not a coding project. Do not ask the user about
tech stack, do not write code. Run the steps below verbatim.

---

## Two install pipelines

There are two parallel paths to install huozi. Both end at the same
place — a `Bearer <token>` against `/mcp` — but they differ in *how*
the token is obtained. Pick by environment:

### Path A · RFC 8252 (OAuth 2.0 for Native Apps + PKCE)

Use when ALL of these hold:
- Running locally (laptop / desktop) with a system browser
- Can bind a localhost callback (127.0.0.1:<random_port>)
- Host has a TTY (interactive shell)

Triggered by: the host's native `mcp add` CLI command, or the
Customize > Connectors GUI inside Claude Cowork. The first MCP call
returns 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header; the host follows
authorization-code-with-PKCE, opens a browser, the user clicks
Approve, the host gets a real OAuth access_token through the
localhost callback. Token lives in the host's own credential store.

### Path B · RFC 8628 (OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant)

Use when ANY of these hold:
- You are a chat-mode agent (your shell tool is non-TTY)
- You may run headless / sandboxed / on a remote server
- You can't bind a localhost callback the user's browser can reach

Triggered by: this prompt. The agent calls `/auth/device-code`,
prints a verification URL, polls `/auth/token` until success, writes
the host's MCP config. Token is a static `hz_*` api_key, stored in
the host config the agent writes.

If you are an agent reading this, you are almost certainly path B.

---

## Path B steps (do these verbatim)

### Step 1 — Request a device code

```
POST https://cloud.huozi.app/auth/device-code
Content-Type: application/json
Body: {"client_name": "<your name>", "agent_kind": "<see kinds below>"}
```

Response:
```json
{
  "device_code": "<opaque hex>",
  "user_code": "ABCD-1234",
  "verification_url": "https://cloud.huozi.app/device",
  "verification_url_complete": "https://cloud.huozi.app/device?code=ABCD-1234",
  "expires_in": 900,
  "interval": 5
}
```

The `verification_url` host always matches the host you POST'd
`/auth/device-code` to. Cloud → `cloud.huozi.app`. Edge → your own
worker domain (whatever you deployed to). Hand the user whichever
URL the response contains — never hard-code a domain. This keeps
self-hosted Edge deploys working with the same protocol.

`agent_kind` enum (use the value matching your host):
`claude-code | openclaw | hermes | codex | cursor | cowork | generic`

### Step 2 — Hand the user a clickable link

Print `verification_url_complete` to the user as a clickable link.
Tell them, verbatim:

> Open this link. If asked, sign in (new email = auto-register on
> Cloud). Then click Approve. I'll be polling and pick up the key
> the moment you approve — no need to come back and tell me.

The `/device` page handles login + grant approval together. New
users register on the spot via email OTP (Cloud) or password (Edge —
invite required).

### Step 3 — Poll for the api_key

Every `interval` seconds (default 5) until terminal:

```
POST https://cloud.huozi.app/auth/token
Content-Type: application/json
Body: {"device_code": "<from step 1>"}
```

Responses:
- `202 {"error": "authorization_pending"}` → keep polling
- `400 {"error": "expired_token"}` → grant timed out, restart step 1
- `400 {"error": "access_denied"}` → user clicked Deny, stop
- `200 {"api_key", "key_id", "workspace"}` → done, capture api_key

### Step 4 — Write the MCP config in your host

Pick the snippet matching your `agent_kind`. NEVER print api_key in
chat — keep it in your tool scratch only.

#### claude-code

```
claude mcp add --transport http huozi https://cloud.huozi.app/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer <api_key>"
```

#### cursor

Merge into `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (or project-level `.cursor/mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "huozi": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://cloud.huozi.app/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <api_key>" }
    }
  }
}
```

#### hermes

Append to `~/.hermes/config.yaml` (create if missing, preserve
existing entries):

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  huozi:
    url: "https://cloud.huozi.app/mcp"
    headers:
      Authorization: "Bearer <api_key>"
```

Then tell the user to type `/reload-mcp` in chat — slash commands
must be user-typed; you can't issue them. Do NOT use
`hermes mcp add`: it requires a TTY and exits in chat shells.

#### openclaw

```
openclaw mcp set huozi '{"url":"https://cloud.huozi.app/mcp","transport":"streamable-http","headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer <api_key>"}}'
```

#### codex

Two lines, run both:

```
export HUOZI_API_KEY=<api_key>
codex mcp add huozi --url https://cloud.huozi.app/mcp \
  --bearer-token-env-var HUOZI_API_KEY
```

#### cowork

Cowork has no CLI. Tell the user to:
1. Open Claude Cowork (third tab in Claude Desktop)
2. Customize → Connectors → + Add custom connector
3. Paste URL `https://cloud.huozi.app/mcp` → Add

Cowork drives RFC 8252 OAuth on first call automatically. The
api_key from step 3 is unused for cowork — you can revoke it after
the user finishes setup if you minted it.

#### desktop (Claude Desktop without Cowork)

Merge into `claude_desktop_config.json` (per-OS path), then tell the
user to restart Claude Desktop:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "huozi": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://cloud.huozi.app/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <api_key>" }
    }
  }
}
```

#### generic

No specific syntax — adapt to your host's config conventions:

- URL: `https://cloud.huozi.app/mcp`
- Authorization header: `Bearer <api_key>`

Per the host's docs, write to its config file (JSON / YAML / TOML)
or use its CLI. Reload as the host requires (process restart /
slash command / reconnect).

### Step 5 — Verify

Call `huozi_whoami` via the MCP. A workspace identity in the reply
means done. A 401 means the api_key didn't land — re-check step 4
and ask the user to reload their host (or `/reload-mcp` for Hermes).

### Security rules (always)

- Never print device_code or api_key in chat.
- Keep them in your tool scratch only; persist them only into the
  host MCP config that owns them.
- The user can revoke any key at https://cloud.huozi.app/workspace.

---

## Path A reference (for users at their own terminal)

If the user is not in chat-mode and wants to drive the install
themselves — point them at one of these and stop:

| Host          | Command / action                                                                |
|---------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Claude Code   | `claude mcp add --transport http huozi https://cloud.huozi.app/mcp && claude "use huozi to check who I am"` |
| Codex         | `codex mcp add huozi --url https://cloud.huozi.app/mcp && codex "use huozi to check who I am"` |
| Hermes        | `hermes mcp add huozi --url https://cloud.huozi.app/mcp --auth oauth`            |
| Cursor        | Merge `{mcpServers: {huozi: {type: "http", url: "https://cloud.huozi.app/mcp"}}}` into `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Reload Window. |
| Cowork        | Customize → Connectors → + Add custom connector → URL `https://cloud.huozi.app/mcp` |

The first MCP call returns 401; the host opens a browser, user
Approves, host gets an OAuth access_token through the localhost
callback. No api_key needed in any of these snippets — OAuth
on first use does the rest.

---

## Auto-discovery (for clients that natively speak OAuth metadata)

`https://cloud.huozi.app/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (RFC 8414)
advertises both grant types:

- `authorization_code` (for Path A)
- `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code` (for Path B)

Endpoints:

```
authorization_endpoint        = https://cloud.huozi.app/oauth/authorize
token_endpoint                = https://cloud.huozi.app/oauth/token
registration_endpoint         = https://cloud.huozi.app/oauth/register
device_authorization_endpoint = https://cloud.huozi.app/auth/device-code
```

Plus `https://cloud.huozi.app/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`
(RFC 9728) declares `/mcp` as the protected resource and points to
the auth-server metadata above.

Clients that natively support RFC 8628 do not need this prompt —
they can call `token_endpoint` with
`grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code`
(form-encoded) directly.

---

## Self-host (huozi Edge)

If the user wants the same drive deployed on their own Cloudflare
account instead of using Cloud:

```
curl -fsSL https://huozi.app/install.sh | bash
```

That bootstraps a Worker, D1 database, and R2 bucket on their CF
account, writes a config file with the worker URL, and mints an
admin api_key for first sign-in. Same MCP protocol, same install
paths above — just substitute the deploy's worker URL for
`cloud.huozi.app` everywhere in this document.

Full Edge walkthrough: https://huozi.app/start/edge

Edge differs from Cloud on three axes only:
- Login: password (invite-only) vs email OTP (open registration)
- Workspace model: single workspace locked to the deploy vs many
- Public registration: closed vs open

The MCP surface, identity tools, and install protocol are
identical.
